explanation: Compared against erdosproblems.com/1132: for an infinite sequence x_1, x_2, … in [−1,1], with L_n(x) = Σ_{k≤n} |l_k(x)| relative to x_1,…,x_n, is limsup L_n(x)/log n ≥ 2/π for almost all x ∈ (−1,1)? The Lean statement: for every injective sequence in [−1,1] (distinctness needed for l_k to be defined), for a.e. t ∈ (−1,1) (volume restricted to Ioo), for every ε > 0 there are infinitely many n with L_n(t) ≥ (2/π − ε) log n, which is equivalent to limsup L_n/log n ≥ 2/π and avoids junk values of a real limsup. lebesgueFunction is defined from the first n nodes, as on the page. Faithful.
